name: validate-luhn
summary: Check whether a numeric string passes the Luhn checksum, as used by credit card numbers and other identifiers.
description: Applies the standard Luhn (mod 10) checksum algorithm to a digit string: doubling every second digit from the rightmost, subtracting 9 from any result over 9, summing all digits, and checking the total is a multiple of 10. This is a checksum-format check only -- it does NOT verify the number belongs to a real, active account, is not stolen, or is authorized for any transaction (none of that is possible without a live call to a card network or issuer, which is not available to any capability under the current ABI whitelist). Luhn validity is necessary but nowhere near sufficient for treating a card number as safe to charge. Formatting characters (spaces, dashes) are stripped before checking when strip_formatting is true (the default); the input is never logged, persisted, or included in the output.

preconditions.description: The caller provides a string in the number field, possibly containing spaces/dashes if strip_formatting is true.

postconditions.description: valid: true means the digit string passes the Luhn checksum, nothing more -- not that it is a real, active, or authorized account number.
The output never contains the input number value, in whole or in part.

side_effects.description: Produces one checksum result derived from the provided number; does not log, persist, or transmit the input.
